newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault sees Valeo solution on track.
newsitem.headline: Renault sees Valeo solution on track.

text.p: Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer said in a radio interview on Saturday he believed negotiations to place Carlo De Benedetti's 28 percent stake in car parts supplier Valeo with a French company were on a positive track.

"I think the solution that has presented itself will probably succeed," he told Radio Classique, referring to an announcement last month by holding company CGIP that it was trying to conclude the purchase of the Valeo stake from De Benedetti's holding company Cerus.
"It would be an enormous disappointment if it didn't go through," Schweitzer said.
Renault and its French rival PSA Peugeot Citroen had said they opposed a takeover of Valeo, their leading supplier, by a foreign competitor.
"I'm not privy to the secrets of the gods, but I have the impression things are on the right track," he said.
Unlike his counterpart at the PSA group, Jacques Calvet, who threatened a boycott if Valeo fell into the wrong hands, Schweitzer said he did not even want to consider such a catastrophic scenario.

"It would mean that Valeo, with all its French facilities, which are our suppliers -- we'd be trying to wipe them off the map the next day. It would be a catastrophe I don't even want to think about," Schweitzer said.
